# Cubli - Electrical/Electronics Technical Schedule

**Generated from `schedule.yaml`. Do not edit this file by hand** - edit the YAML and run `python electrical/generate_schedule.py`.

Day 1 = 2026-07-23 - day 29 = 2026-08-20. Electrical work starts 2026-07-28 (day 6), three days behind the original plan.

## Hardware baseline

**3 complete actuation sets, 0 spares. Strategy: TRIAGE THREE, COMMISSION ONE.**

The 1-DoF rig is NOT permanent. It is built from one of the three cube sets and must be STRIPPED at EL-21 during Phase 2 to populate the third cube axis (3-4 Aug). There is no independent bench after 4 Aug, so Phase 3 brake work runs on the cube itself. Any motor, driver or encoder failure after integration loses an axis with no resupply before 20 Aug.

### Phase 1 scope and exit criteria

**EL-11 Bench supply, e-stop and fuse loop**

Bench PSU set up as the only energy source for all Phase 1 work. Verify the current limit trips against a known resistive load before the inline fuse blows. E-stop and fuse wired into the bench loop. LiPo safety kit staged (charger, safe bag, cell alarm) but the battery stays out of the loop until EL-25.

- Materials: bench PSU, e-stop/anti-spark switch, inline fuse - MUST BUY (PROCUREMENT.md)
- **Exit:** PSU current limit demonstrably trips at its set value before the inline fuse opens, verified on a known load. E-stop opens the bus in one action.

**EL-12 Triage three - incoming inspection of all actuation sets**

TRIAGE THREE, COMMISSION ONE. Smoke-test all three motor/driver/encoder sets early so a dead unit surfaces now, not at integration: phase continuity and resistance against the 194 mOhm datasheet figure, moteus-n1 boot and enumerate, MA600 SPI read-back, and assign a distinct CAN ID to each of the three drivers. No commissioning beyond this - one set only goes forward to EL-13.

- Materials: scrap-sourceable (existing BOM hardware only)
- **Exit:** 3 of 3 sets: phase-to-phase resistance within +/-20% of 194 mOhm on all three pairs, driver enumerates on CAN-FD at its assigned unique ID, MA600 returns a changing 16-bit angle with no error flag. Any set failing is logged as a dead unit - with zero spares this is escalated same day.

**EL-13 Commission one - driver, motor and phase wiring**

Fully commission set #1 through to the rig. Phase wiring terminated (bullet connectors, heat-shrink), moteus-n1 firmware current, FOC calibration run against the MA600, CAN ID fixed and recorded. All on the current-limited bench PSU.

- Materials: bullet connectors, heat-shrink, 14 AWG - MUST BUY
- **Exit:** moteus-n1 completes FOC calibration with no fault, holds a commanded current within 5% of setpoint, and commutates the motor smoothly through a full mechanical revolution in both directions.

**EL-15 5 V rail trim and load characterisation**

LM2596 buck trimmed to 5.00 V. Characterise the rail under load to 1.5 A: output voltage vs load, ripple, and module thermals logged. 1N5819 back-feed diode fitted. 100 uF/16 V on the 5 V rail only. Establishes the rail budget before the servo is added in Phase 3.

- Materials: LM2596 + caps + diode from BOM; heatsink scrap-sourceable
- **Exit:** Rail measures 5.00 V +/-0.05 V at no load and holds >= 4.75 V at 1.5 A. Ripple recorded in mV pk-pk. LM2596 case temperature logged at 1.5 A steady state and stated in degC.

**EL-14 MA600 off-axis encoder installation and calibration**

Bond the ring magnet to the wheel hub. Set the air gap with a shim stack to <= 0.5 mm with the chip centred on the 4 mm magnet thickness - record the shim value, it becomes the assembly spec for every axis at EL-21. SPI cable run kept under 20 cm. Bias trim and encoder recalibration after bonding.

- Materials: scrap-sourceable (shim stock); ring magnet from BOM
- **Exit:** Measured air gap <= 0.5 mm recorded as a numeric shim value, SPI run < 20 cm, and the encoder returns monotonic absolute angle over a full revolution with zero error flags across a 10-minute spin.

**EL-16 Rig harness and 2-node CAN-FD bus**

Rig harness: bench PSU to driver via XT30 (each moteus ships a mating XT30, so the connector side is covered), CAN-FD from driver to Teensy 4.1. 2-node bus, linear, split termination 2x 60.4 ohm + 4.7 nF at the two physical ends. BMI270 on I2C to the Teensy, mounted on the rig body. Tethered operation - no telemetry link in Phase 1.

- Materials: 60.4 ohm resistors, 4.7 nF caps from BOM; JST-PH3 cable gauge is a TODO
- **Exit:** Unpowered resistance across CANH-CANL reads 60 ohm +/-3 ohm. Driver and Teensy both enumerate at 5 Mbps. BMI270 returns live accel and gyro on I2C at the configured ODR.

**EL-17 Parameter characterisation - Kt, J, friction, latency**

Electrical measurement setup for the four parameters the control workstream needs: Kt by current step against measured torque (expect 0.02513 N m/A), wheel inertia J by spin-down, viscous and Coulomb friction by coast-down, and closed-loop latency by command-to-encoder timestamp. Provide the instrumentation; the numbers are consumed downstream.

- **Exit:** Four numbers delivered with units and uncertainty: Kt in N m/A (compare against 0.02513 nominal), J in kg m^2, viscous and Coulomb friction coefficients, and loop latency in ms. Each measured, not assumed.

**EL-18 Board outline and connector positions**

HARD 1 AUG EXTERNAL DATE - gates the C5 mass freeze and the C11 frame print. Fix the three driver positions from the MA600 SPI < 20 cm rule (encoder position dictates driver position, not the reverse). Fix the CAN routing as a linear chain across three drivers plus Teensy with stubs < 10 cm and the two physical bus ends identified. Perfboard floorplan on the 15 x 9 cm double-sided board: 25 V bus in, LM2596, 5 V rail, bulk cap footprint, Teensy, XIAO ESP32-C6, BMI270, servo header, CAN termination. Issue outline, mounting holes, keep-out heights, connector positions and exit directions.

- Note: Not on the G3 critical path but carries a harder external date than G3 itself. If EL-14 slips, issue from the layout study with conservative keep-outs rather than delay - a late outline cascades to G5.
- **Exit:** Outline issued as a dimensioned drawing with every connector position and exit direction fixed, on 1 Aug. Board mass estimate stated in grams (TODO - requires weighing the populated proto, see open questions).

**EL-19 Closed-loop rig bring-up**

Teensy + BMI270 + CAN-FD closed loop on the 1-DoF rig. Bench PSU, tethered. Verify the disarm path and watchdog trip before any balance attempt. Support controller tuning to a sustained balance.

- **Exit:** Rig balances >= 60 s unassisted on the bench PSU. Watchdog trips the driver to a safe state within its configured timeout, verified by deliberately stalling the control loop. Zero CAN error frames during the balance run.

### Phase 2 scope and exit criteria

**EL-21 Replicate actuation sets 2 and 3** *[CARRIED]*

Identical to EL-13 and EL-14, replicated on the remaining two sets: phase wiring, FOC calibration, CAN ID, magnet bonding and gap to the EL-14 shim spec. No new engineering - the procedure is fixed and the numbers are known. INCLUDES STRIPPING THE 1-DoF RIG: with three sets and no spare, the rig's set becomes the third cube axis. The bench rig ceases to exist at this point.

- Materials: scrap-sourceable (BOM hardware, already triaged at EL-12)
- **Exit:** 3 of 3 sets FOC-calibrated with unique CAN IDs, each encoder at <= 0.5 mm gap matching the recorded EL-14 shim value, each returning monotonic angle with no error flags.

**EL-23 Battery power chain** *[NEW]*

Does not exist in the 1-DoF rig, which ran entirely on a bench PSU. XT90 battery lead, anti-spark switch, e-stop, inline fuse sized to the bus, and bulk capacitance 470-1000 uF at >= 50 V for regen transients. The BOM 100 uF parts are 16 V and must never appear on this rail.

- Materials: Bulk cap SCRAP-SOURCED per invariant (470-1000 uF, >= 50 V). XT90 pair in BOM. E-stop/anti-spark switch and fuse MUST BUY. If no scrap cap >= 50 V is found, this task has no defined transient path - see open questions.
- **Exit:** Bulk capacitance >= 470 uF at >= 50 V fitted and its working voltage verified by part marking. Fuse rating stated in amps and justified against the 48 A transient. Anti-spark switch limits inrush - measured peak inrush current recorded in A.

**EL-24 Power/signal distribution perfboard** *[NEW]*

DECIDED: perfboard, not a fabricated PCB. The rig had point-to-point wiring and no distribution board at all. Two ground domains with exactly one star point. 5 V rail split so the servo has a separate supply from the logic. 25 V bus in, LM2596, bulk cap, Teensy, XIAO ESP32-C6, BMI270, servo header, CAN split termination - all to the EL-18 floorplan.

- **Exit:** Continuity check confirms exactly one connection between the two ground domains (the star point) - measured, not assumed. Logic 5 V and servo 5 V are separately isolatable. Zero 16 V-rated part present on the 25 V bus, verified by inspection against part markings before power.

**EL-22 4-node CAN-FD bus** *[SCALED]*

Same protocol and bit rate as the EL-16 rig bus, but 2 nodes -> 4 (three drivers + Teensy). Linear topology across the cube geometry, every stub < 10 cm, split termination moved to the two new physical bus ends. Error soak at full rate with all four nodes addressed.

- Scaling: 2 nodes -> 4 nodes; bus length grows from bench to cube geometry
- **Exit:** Unpowered CANH-CANL reads 60 ohm +/-3 ohm with termination at the two ends only. All 4 nodes enumerate at 5 Mbps. Zero error frames over a 30-minute soak with all three drivers commanded.

**EL-26 Harness fabrication and routing** *[SCALED]*

The rig had one short bench harness. The cube needs a full distribution harness: XT90 battery lead to three XT30 driver drops at 14 AWG, CAN chain, three SPI runs each under 20 cm, I2C to the IMU. Routed clear of the wheels, strain-relieved and labelled. Each moteus ships a mating XT30 so the connector side is covered.

- Materials: 14 AWG and 24-26 AWG wire MUST BUY; XT30 mating halves ship with the moteus
- **Exit:** Every SPI run measured < 20 cm and every CAN stub < 10 cm, recorded per axis. All power joints pull-tested. No conductor within the wheel sweep envelope, verified by rotating each wheel through a full revolution by hand.

**EL-27 Telemetry link** *[NEW]*

Untethered operation is mandatory on a balancing cube - a tether applies a disturbance torque and can catch. The rig was tethered throughout, so this has no Phase 1 equivalent. XIAO ESP32-C6 on the logic 5 V rail, UART to the Teensy, antenna clear of the frame. TX bursts draw ~300 mA and must not disturb the logic rail.

- **Exit:** Live telemetry received with the cube fully untethered at >= 2 m range. Logic 5 V rail sag during a 300 mA TX burst measured and < 100 mV. Packet loss stated as a percentage over a 5-minute run.

**EL-25 48 A transient handling and first battery power-on** *[SCALED]*

The rig ran one motor at up to 16 A on a current-limited PSU. The cube runs three at once: 48 A transient on a battery with no current limit. Verify bus sag and bulk cap behaviour under a simultaneous three-axis current step. FIRST BATTERY CONNECTION of the project - anti-spark, fuse verified, cell alarm on, fire-safe area, second person present.

- Scaling: 16 A single-axis on a limited PSU -> 48 A three-axis on an unlimited battery
- **Exit:** Bus holds >= 20 V at the 48 A three-axis transient (measured at the board, not the battery terminals). Inrush on connection recorded in A. No fuse opening, no driver undervoltage fault.

**EL-28 Thermal behaviour of three drivers in an enclosed volume** *[NEW]*

The rig ran one driver in free air on a bench. The cube encloses three drivers plus the LM2596 in a sealed printed volume with no forced convection. Characterise the steady-state rise under a representative balance load and confirm nothing is thermally throttling or drifting.

- Scaling: 1 driver in free air -> 3 drivers + buck in a sealed volume
- Materials: scrap-sourceable (thermocouple or IR thermometer)
- **Exit:** Driver and LM2596 case temperatures logged over a 20-minute balance- representative load; steady state reached with every device below its rated limit, and the peak value stated in degC per device.

**EL-29 Integrated power-on and axis addressability** *[CARRIED]*

Same bring-up sequence as EL-19, replicated across three axes on the integrated cube. Continuity and isolation before power, PSU smoke test with wheels removed, PSU test with wheels at a low current limit, then battery. Every MA600 re-checked at the EL-14 gap spec after mechanical assembly - the gap drifts during integration.

- **Exit:** All 3 axes addressable from the flight computer on battery power, all 3 encoders reading within the <= 0.5 mm gap spec after assembly, IMU live, telemetry up. Zero CAN error frames during a full three-axis open-loop spin.

## Phase 3 - Brake actuation electrical -> G8

Days 19-27 (10 Aug - 18 Aug), 5 tasks.

| ID | Task | Days | Dates | Depends on |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| EL-31 | Servo isolated 5 V rail and drive circuit | 19-20 | 10 Aug - 11 Aug | EL-29 |
| EL-32 | Rail stability under servo stall | 20-21 | 11 Aug - 12 Aug | EL-31 |
| EL-33 | Brake closure-time measurement | 23-24 | 14 Aug - 15 Aug | EL-32 |
| EL-34 | Spin-down brake-torque measurement | 24-26 | 15 Aug - 17 Aug | EL-33 |
| EL-35 | Jump-up electrical support | 26-27 | 17 Aug - 18 Aug | EL-34 |

### Phase 3 scope and exit criteria

**EL-31 Servo isolated 5 V rail and drive circuit**

TowerPro MG92B on the isolated servo 5 V rail established at EL-24, separate from the logic supply. PWM signal only from the Teensy - no servo current through the logic ground. Flyback protection on the servo supply. Local decoupling at the servo header.

- Materials: MG92B and diode from BOM; decoupling caps from BOM
- **Exit:** Servo sweeps its full commanded range on 50 Hz PWM. Logic rail disturbance during a servo step measured and < 100 mV. Flyback path verified present by inspection and by scoping the servo supply at switch-off.

**EL-32 Rail stability under servo stall**

The brake holds a barrier against a spinning wheel, so the servo stalls by design rather than as a fault. Verify the isolated rail survives a sustained stall without browning out the logic domain or the LM2596.

- **Exit:** Servo stall current measured in A. Servo rail holds >= 4.75 V and the logic rail holds >= 4.9 V throughout a 5-second sustained stall. LM2596 case temperature during stall recorded in degC.

**EL-33 Brake closure-time measurement**

Instrument the brake actuation timing on the scope: PWM command edge to mechanical barrier contact. The jump-up needs a near-impulsive momentum transfer, so closure time is a control-loop input, not a comfort number.

- Scheduling: Deliberately placed AFTER the G6 edge-balance gate on 13 Aug. Brake work is the sacrificial item by standing decision - it never competes with edge balance for time on the cube.
- **Exit:** Closure time from command edge to barrier contact measured in ms, averaged over >= 10 actuations with the spread stated.

**EL-34 Spin-down brake-torque measurement**

Measure the actual braking torque from wheel spin-down against the barrier: log wheel speed through the braking event and differentiate. The stated 5.0 N m in the sizing work has no measured provenance (AUDIT.md M-5) and beta depends on it directly - this task is where that number gets a source.

- **Exit:** Brake torque measured in N m from logged spin-down, stated with uncertainty, and compared explicitly against the 5.0 N m assumed in the sizing.

**EL-35 Jump-up electrical support**

Support the jump-up attempt: brake circuit live, spin-up to the design wheel speed of 733 rad/s, bus and rail monitoring through the release transient. This is the largest single energy event the electrical system sees.

- **Exit:** Brake commands and releases on demand through a full jump-up attempt with no bus overvoltage fault and no driver fault logged. Peak bus voltage during the release transient recorded in V.

### G5 - Cube integrated - day 18 (9 Aug)

Longest path from the electrical start:

```
EL-11 (d6-6) -> EL-12 (d6-7) -> EL-13 (d7-8) -> EL-14 (d8-9) ->
    EL-17 (d9-10) -> EL-19 (d10-11) -> EL-21 (d12-13) -> EL-22 (d14-14) ->

```

**Float on G5: 0 day(s) - ZERO FLOAT.** Path ends day 18, gate is day 18.

ZERO FLOAT. The binding chain runs through the bus, harness and battery transient, not the board: EL-21 (replicate sets) -> EL-22 (4-node bus) -> EL-26 (harness) -> EL-25 (48 A transient / first battery power-on) -> EL-29 (integrated power-on). EL-24 (perfboard) finishes day 13 and feeds EL-22 with a day to spare, so the perfboard is NOT the pinch - the harness and the battery bring-up are. Phase 2 inherits every day of Phase 1 slip directly, because EL-21 cannot start until the rig is proven at EL-19.

EL-28 (thermal) shares the same predecessor EL-25 and also ends day 18 with zero float, so G5 has two independent zero-float finishers.

## Issues found

### I-1 (BLOCKER) - Three actuation sets kills the permanent bench rig

The brief's invariant "4 complete sets, so the 1-DoF rig survives as a permanent bench" is not achievable - you confirmed three sets. The rig is built from a cube set and must be stripped at EL-21 on 3 Aug. Consequences carried into this schedule: TRIAGE FOUR becomes TRIAGE THREE; there is no independent bench after 4 Aug, so all Phase 3 brake work runs on the flight article; and any post-integration failure of a motor, driver or encoder loses an axis permanently with no resupply before 20 Aug.

**Action required:** RISKS.md RE11 needs rewriting - "fewer than four sets" is no longer a risk, it is the baseline. The replacement is a no-spare risk at higher severity. AUDIT.md and PLAN.md still carry the 4-set premise in places.

### I-2 (BLOCKER) - Zero float on all three gates

G3, G5 and G8 each close with exactly zero float. This is a direct consequence of the electrical workstream starting on day 6 rather than day 3 - three days were lost before any electrical work began, and there is nowhere in a 22-day remaining span to recover them. No task has been compressed to manufacture slack.

**Action required:** Accept the zero float explicitly, or cut scope. The candidates for cutting are named in I-3.

### I-3 (MAJOR) - EL-18 board outline has a harder date than the gate it sits under

EL-18 must issue on 1 Aug because it gates the C5 mass freeze and the C11 frame print, both of which feed G5 on 9 Aug. It sits in Phase 1 but does not serve G3. It depends on EL-14 (encoder installation, ends 31 Jul), which is itself on the zero-float G3 critical path. A one-day slip on EL-14 therefore threatens both G3 and the 1 Aug external commitment simultaneously.

**Action required:** Standing fallback: if EL-14 slips, issue EL-18 from the layout study with conservative keep-outs rather than delaying it. A late outline cascades further than a slightly oversized one.

### I-4 (MAJOR) - Phase 3 brake work has no bench and cannot start before G6

With the rig stripped, EL-31 and EL-32 run on the integrated cube during 10-12 Aug - the same window as edge-balance work ahead of the G6 hard kill date on 13 Aug. EL-33 onward is scheduled after G6 to protect it, which is why days 22 is left clear. If edge balance consumes 10-13 Aug entirely, EL-31 and EL-32 slip into the G6-to-G8 window and the Phase 3 chain loses its structured margin.

**Action required:** Confirm the standing decision holds: brake work is sacrificial and yields to edge balance without discussion on the day.

### I-5 (MAJOR) - Bulk capacitance is scrap-sourced with no fallback

The invariant states the 470-1000 uF >= 50 V bulk cap comes from scrap. PROCUREMENT.md carries it as a to-buy line. EL-23 and therefore EL-25 (48 A transient, first battery power-on) have no defined transient path if no suitable scrap part is found. The BOM 100 uF parts are 16 V and cannot substitute.

**Action required:** Confirm a >= 50 V part exists in scrap before 3 Aug, or convert this to a purchase line with the lead time checked against the 3 Aug EL-23 start.

### I-6 (MINOR) - Design wheel speed differs between the brief and the repository

The brief states a design wheel speed of 733 rad/s (7000 rpm). The repository closed this on 28 Jul at 6000 rpm = 628 rad/s (MOTOR_SPEED.md, AUDIT.md M-4), describing 733 rad/s as the superseded BOM figure. This schedule uses the brief's 733 rad/s in EL-35 because it was given as an invariant, but the two documents now disagree.

**Action required:** Confirm which figure governs. It changes the spin-up target in EL-35 and the stored energy the brake must absorb in EL-34.
